messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED — alert: prod-kv-cache: reuse_rate spike + p99 latency climb across us-west-2 inference pools. Auto-created from Pager rule #kv-reuse-500.

Alex: seeing OOMs and 503s on a subset of endpoints, started ~12:03 UTC. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv/kv-reuse?orgId=1&from=now-30m&to=now — big spike in kv-cache entries per worker. logs attached: `kv_cache.cpp:237 stale_seq_offset detected for req=0x7f9a` repeated.

Priya: acked, I'm oncall. Paging SRE+Runtime. @Ben @Jamie can you join?

Ben: looking. my quick read — continuous batching + kv reuse path looks like it's reusing KV entries across request boundaries when sequence offsets mismatch. that explains both stale values and sudden memory growth.

Jamie: on my way. can we throttle batching or disable reuse as hotfix?

Alex: I can reproduce locally with stress runner: sequence offsets slip when head padding is applied + partial kv invalidation. repro script:

```
# repro sketch
for i in range(1000):
  send_request(seq_offset=(i % 4))
  # occasionally do partial attention mask
```

Ben: actionable mitigation options (short list):
- flip feature flag `runtime.enable_kv_reuse` -> false (fastest)
- flush KV cache on request boundary in runtime (safer hotfix)
- revert recent batching config that increased max_batch_size & allowed cross-model batching

Priya: do flag flip first. ask infra to roll that across us-west-2 pools only. reduces perf but should stop leak.

Sasha: I can roll the flag. running the console patch now. command: `redwood-config set runtime.enable_kv_reuse false --env=prod --region=us-west-2`

deploy-bot: flag change started by Sasha — rollout id flag-roll-2204. Rolling to 50% of hosts in us-west-2.

Laura: I'm watching metrics. p99 came down slightly but mem still climbing on a few hosts. might be leftover stale entries; we should flush caches too.

Ben: agree — while flag rolls, prepare a targeted hotfix: zero kv pointer on reply boundary and validate seq offsets before reuse. small patch:

```
- if (kv.seq_offset == cached.seq_offset) {
-   reuse_cache();
- }
+ if (kv.seq_offset == cached.seq_offset && within_session_bounds(req)) {
+   reuse_cache();
+ } else {
+   cached.clear(); // ensure no cross-request leakage
+ }
```

Jamie: I'll cut a canary build with that guard and a forced cache-clear after each request for the canary hosts.

Priya: prioritize canary on the same hosts still showing mem growth. Sasha coordinate with deploy-bot. also please set a customer-impact note.

Sasha: deploying canary build cb-2204-hotfix to 4 canary hosts in us-west-2 now.

deploy-bot: deploy started — cb-2204-hotfix -> canary group cw-usw2-4.

Alex: when can we expect observability to show improvement? looking at traces, cross-request leakage leads to wrong logits occasionally — some responses look like mixed contexts.

Laura: traces/requests sampling shows ~12% requests on affected hosts had payload contamination. support tickets coming in.

Priya: customer impact summary so far: ~20 customers experienced degraded outputs or 5xxs in last 45m. 3 escalations flagged as high (NovaPay, BrightHealth, AtlasML). Support lead informed.

Sasha: canary metrics: memory stable on 3/4 hosts after hotfix, p99 latency improved ~15% on canaries, error rate dropped to baseline.

Ben: good. next step: roll hotfix to remaining affected hosts, but keep kv_reuse flag off until we add a stronger correctness test coverage.

Jamie: rolling cb-2204-hotfix to remaining us-west-2 affected pool now. this will keep batching intact but avoid reuse bug.

deploy-bot: rollout cb-2204-hotfix -> affected-pool-usw2 initiated by Jamie. 25% -> 50% -> 100% staged.

incident-bot: Pager escalation: SRE escalation completed. Priority set to P1 -> P2 as mitigation is holding, still monitoring.

Priya: contacting customer success for NovaPay + BrightHealth to provide timeline and mitigation notes. Sasha, can you attach a short write-up for CS?

Sasha: adding notes to ticket INS-2204: cause: KV reuse correctness bug (stale seq offsets + cross-request leakage). mitigation: disabled kv_reuse flag; deployed hotfix cb-2204 to affected hosts; running post-rollback tests and extra canaries. ETA for full roll: 30m.

Alex: one weird finding — some model variants that had longer prefix lengths showed worse contamination. possible order-of-ops where prefix padding wasn't considered in seq offset calculation. we should add unit tests for padding awareness.

Ben: assigning follow-ups: Alex -> root cause & tests, Jamie -> runtime guard & integration test, Sasha -> rollout playbook & CS notes, Laura -> metrics dashboards + alert tuning.

Priya: oncall handoff in 40m — @Laura will take over monitoring for next shift. I'm staying on to make sure CS is briefed.

Laura: taking handoff at 12:45 UTC. I'll keep an eye on mem and p99.

Alex: quick todo to avoid recurrence: add seq-offset validation failure metric, increase sampling of traces for cross-request tokens, and add CI fuzz for random padding lengths.

Ben: agreed. also we should consider a short-term GA: add a safety when batcher and reuse are enabled together — runtime should default to conservative reuse.

deploy-bot: rollout cb-2204-hotfix -> affected-pool-usw2 completed successfully. no regressions detected during 10m smoke.

Sasha: final customer impact update posted to INS-2204 and CS notified. I'll open a postmortem doc and link it here.

Priya: thanks team. P1->P2 demoted, still monitoring. good job on quick coordination. :thumbsup:

Alex: I'll start the postmortem draft. tagging Ben/Jamie/Sasha for technical write-up.

incident-bot: Incident INS-2204: status = mitigated, severity = P2, assigned -> Alex, Ben, Jamie.

Laura: taking over monitoring; if anything spikes I'll reopen pager.

Ben: follow-up action items created in the incident tracker.

Jamie: leaving notes in runtime repo with patch id rtm-2204-guard.

Sasha: closing thread here, moving discussion to postmortem doc.

deploy-bot: NOTE: rollback tool remains available at /internal/deploys if we need to revert cb-2204-hotfix.

Priya: end of thread.
